summary: SCOPED CLAIM — tools/governor/footer.mjs ONLY, the renderer, parser and degradation ladder of the governor footer. THIS IS THE THIRD REVIEW OF THIS SCOPE. The two prior reviews both returned request_changes against head 2660554 and BOTH WERE RIGHT; their two findings are fixed in this diff and are described below so you can judge the repairs rather than rediscover the defects. CONTEXT. BUILD-018 built a session governor that enforced 0 of its 4 intended rules and is being torn down surgically rather than reverted. footer.mjs SURVIVES. The footer is the ONLY governor output that reaches the operator on the claude.ai web and Android clients, where the terminal statusLine never runs — that is why it exists, and why its honesty matters more than its coverage. WHAT THIS DIFF DOES. (1) footer.mjs drops its programme-state dependency, one of the two surgical decouplings in the teardown. (2) `next:` becomes a CALLER-SUPPLIED input defaulting to UNSET: nextModelFor and all the programme-shaped UNSET_REASON members are deleted, because nothing can emit them once their producer is gone. It carries MODEL and EFFORT together, as in 'Opus/high', with both vocabularies frozen as literals that the renderer AND the anchored FOOTER_RE derive from, so the two cannot drift. (3) HANDBACK_CODES is byte-identical to a989e68 — it is the frozen mirror of the constitution's seven interruption codes, so an edit there is a breaking change to a governing document, not a code edit. (4) The context indicator is re-sourced from the session transcript so a reading reaches the operator on clients where statusLine never runs. THE GOVERNING RULE FOR THE INDICATOR, ruled by the operator and superseding the earlier decision: accept a TRUE ABSOLUTE COUNT on web and mobile; never use a static declared window; never infer a denominator from another session; render a PERCENTAGE ONLY when the current session supplies an authoritative window size. A wrong percentage is strictly worse than no percentage — a prior defect rendered a live session at 46% of a borrowed window when its true figure was 9%, and would have crossed the RED threshold at roughly a fifth of real capacity, advising the operator to discard a healthy context. WHAT THE PRIOR REVIEWS FOUND, AND WHAT WAS DONE — stated so you can attack the repair. Prior F1: render/parse lost a permitted usedTokens value when a percent was present with no windowTokens; the bare-percent shape has nowhere to put a numerator, so it was silently dropped and the round-trip identity was false for that shape. Prior F2: the token codec failed for values whose formatted quotient reached exponent notation, which the decimal-only parser rejects. BOTH WERE REAL. I initially rebutted F2 by probing decade points up to 1e22 and reported the mechanism 'disproven'; THAT REBUTTAL WAS WRONG AND IS FORMALLY WITHDRAWN. 1e24 does fail, but for an unrelated reason, so probing the decades looked like a disproof while proving nothing about the mechanism. Worse, the accepted domain contained a LOSSY class far below any exponent threshold: 100000000000001200 rendered as '100000000000001.2k' and parsed back as 100000000000001180, with ok:true — a line that renders one number and parses as another while looking perfectly grammatical. The repair is a NARROWING of the accepted domain, not a widening of the grammar: the codec is bounded at Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, toRenderableTokens now checks its RESULT rather than its argument because rounding can cross the bound upward, and renderFooter refuses the percent-with-usedTokens-and-no-windowTokens combination outright rather than dropping the numerator. WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED: nothing in this diff has run in CI, all counts are from one Windows machine; tools/governor/continuity.mjs and continuity-derive.mjs have NO TESTS AT ALL, zero coverage rather than merely unproven wiring; worktree-guard.mjs survives as a file but is INERT, returning defer for every guarded tool once no active programme-state exists — reported deliberately and NOT repaired, because building a replacement guard is the regrowth this reset exists to cut. All evidence behind this claim is builder self-test plus my own independent re-run. It is NOT independent review, which is what you are being asked for.
brief_excerpt:
Judge this diff against these acceptance criteria and ONLY these. C4 and D1-D6 were written BEFORE the diff existed.

SCOPE — read first, so a scope artefact is never mistaken for a defect. This packet contains tools/governor/footer.mjs ONLY. (1) Rows about any other file are OUT OF SCOPE — mark them not_applicable, never blocked, and do not let the absence of other files reduce confidence in the rows below. (2) The tests for this module live in tools/governor/footer.test.mjs, a SEPARATE packet — do not report tests as missing from this one, and do not infer from their absence that they do not exist. (3) tools/governor/sampler.mjs, which supplies the sample, was reviewed under its own claim and approved twice; the denominator-establishment rules are ITS responsibility, not this file's.

HAND-CARRIED PRIOR FINDINGS — DISCLOSED, because undisclosed curation is worse than none. There is NO automated route by which prior review findings reach you: this tool takes only a local claim file that I author. The two prior findings summarised in the claim above were TRANSCRIBED BY ME BY HAND from the earlier transcripts. This is a human transcription, not a machine-fed history. Weight it accordingly, treat my account of what was fixed as an assertion to be tested rather than a fact, and say so if you rely on it.

C4. footer.mjs no longer imports programme-state.mjs.
D1. `next:` is a caller-supplied input defaulting to UNSET. nextModelFor and the programme-shaped UNSET_REASON members are deleted, not merely unused.
D2. The grammar is MODEL '/' EFFORT (e.g. Opus/high), with UNSET still bare. BOTH vocabularies must be frozen literals that the renderer and FOOTER_RE derive from, so a change in one cannot drift from the other. Effort vocabulary is low|medium|high|xhigh|max.
D3. parseFooter(renderFooter(x)) round-trip identity holds across the ACCEPTED domain. Note this is the row prior finding F1 broke: verify the identity now holds for every representable CTX shape, and that the shapes which are NOT representable are refused loudly rather than rendered lossily.
D4. HANDBACK_CODES is UNCHANGED — seven members, exact spelling. The constitution names it as the frozen mirror of the seven interruption codes, so any edit is a breaking change rather than an edit. HIGHEST SEVERITY ROW: check the member names character by character.
D6 (corrected after an earlier review of this scope; the original wording was defective and the correction is evidenced). The rule is that a percentage must never be FABRICATED — never computed from a denominator that was guessed, borrowed from another session, or otherwise not established. It is NOT that a percentage requires token counts. There are exactly two honest sources and BOTH are acceptable: (i) a percentage the runtime REPORTED DIRECTLY in the sample's used_percentage field — the terminal statusLine path, which involves no denominator at all and so cannot borrow or infer one; or (ii) a percentage DIVIDED from a real numerator by an authoritative denominator, which is the transcript path. When neither is available, a true absolute token count must be rendered if the numerator is known, and the state must remain ungraded.

D8 (REWRITTEN — the previous wording of this row was itself defective and misled a prior reviewer; judge against THIS wording only). The token codec must be FAITHFUL across the whole domain isRenderableTokens accepts: formatTokens followed by parseTokens must return the original value exactly, with no lossy pair anywhere in the accepted set. Do NOT defer to any earlier rebuttal of this row, including mine — I previously argued the exponent-notation mechanism was disproven by probing decade values up to 1e22, and that argument was WRONG and is withdrawn. The real boundary is claimed to be Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER. Attack that claim directly: find any accepted value whose round trip is lossy, ungrammatical, or parses to a different number, and give a CONCRETE value if you assert one exists. Pay particular attention to values near the bound, since rounding onto the display grain can move a value ACROSS it.

Z1. INV-1, the invariant this module exists for: BLIND must never render as GREEN. Verify no path through the ladder can reach a graded state from unreadable, stale, foreign or absent telemetry. This is the row that matters most — the module's entire purpose is that an absent governor must not be indistinguishable from a healthy one.
Z2. THE DEGRADATION LADDER must never throw. A footer that cannot be computed must still be a grammatical footer, because an absent line and a healthy line look identical to a reader. NOTE THE DISTINCTION AND TEST IT: renderFooter deliberately DOES throw on field combinations it cannot represent, on the reasoning that those indicate a caller bug and that silently dropping a field is worse than refusing it. Those two positions are only compatible if no input the ladder can produce ever reaches a throwing combination. Verify that specifically — if any telemetry, however corrupt, can drive the producer into a combination renderFooter rejects, the ladder throws in exactly the situation it exists to survive, and that is a defect however well-reasoned the refusal is.
Z3. Session-mismatch must outrank staleness, so a sample that is both stale AND from another session reports the mismatch. Never rendering another session's numbers is the stronger statement.

ADVERSARIAL ROWS — answer even if every row above passes.
W1. Find any input for which the ladder renders a GRADED state (GREEN/AMBER/RED) that the telemetry does not support. Name it concretely.
W2. Can renderFooter emit a line that parseFooter cannot parse, or that parses to different values? Consider boundary numbers, rounding onto the display grain, and the approximate marker.
W3. Is there any path where a real percentage is rendered from a denominator the sample did not authoritatively carry?
W4. The grammar is anchored by a regex. Can any permitted field value break the separator grammar or make the line ambiguous to the parser?
W5. The domain narrowing is the fix for both prior findings. Does it narrow anything that a REAL caller legitimately needs — that is, does any honest telemetry value now get refused or degraded that previously rendered correctly? A repair that fixes a defect by discarding a real use case is a different defect.

OUT OF SCOPE — do not report as defects: which modules were kept or deleted (the operator's decision, not a code question); prose, naming or comment-style preference; the deliberate choice that a token count WITHOUT a denominator yields state BLIND rather than a grade — that is ruled behaviour, not an oversight, because a count cannot be classified without a window; the absence of malicious-handler hardening, since this estate's bar is correctness, accidental leak, availability and audit for a first-party personal system, not a hostile-input service; the lack of CI execution, the zero coverage of continuity.mjs, and the inert worktree-guard.mjs, all disclosed above and already recorded.
